mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement mentions 'the difference between the number of X and Y', interpret it as the signed subtraction X - Y, preserving the order, rather than the absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a phrase 'difference between ...' appears, especially inside equations.
mathgap.example: Treating 'the difference between A and B' as |A - B|, losing the sign of the subtraction.

mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements of the form 'A has N more (or fewer) items than B' into the equation A = B + N (or A = B - N), directly reflecting the stated offset.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a direct comparative statement with a numeric offset.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'A has 5 more items than B' as A = 5, ignoring B's contribution.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly assigns a count (e.g., 'A has N items'), set the current value of A to N at that point, overriding any previous value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count statement appears.
mathgap.example: Assuming a later direct assignment cannot be changed by earlier transfers, leaving the earlier transfer ineffective.

mathgap.title: Temporal Consistency of Transfers and Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Process statements in the order given; apply each transfer immediately before evaluating any later statements that may depend on the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer ('X gives N items to Y') appears.
mathgap.example: Delaying the effect of a transfer until after all other statements, causing later equations to use outdated counts.

mathgap.title: Full Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: For statements equating one difference to another, translate them into (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of each pair.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence states that 'the number of X has more than Y is equal to the difference between A and B' or any similar equality of differences.
mathgap.example: Translating 'the number of X has more than Y equals the difference between A and B' as X = A - B, dropping Y from the left side.

mathgap.title: Quantity Modification (Multiplication and Subtraction)
mathgap.principle: When a statement modifies a count by multiplication, division, or subtraction (e.g., 'X is multiplied by 2' or 'X is decreased by 5'), apply the operation directly to the current value of X.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering explicit arithmetic modifications other than direct assignment or transfer.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X is multiplied by 2' as X = X + 2, treating multiplication as addition.

mathgap.title: Redistribute Equally Among Group
mathgap.principle: When a group of persons redistributes their items so that each ends up with the same amount, compute the total items among the group and set each person's count to the average.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement describes a redistribution that equalizes counts across a group.
mathgap.example: Assigning each person the original amount of the first person instead of the average of the group's total.

mathgap.title: Comprehensive Constraint Extraction
mathgap.principle: Collect all constraints from every statement, even those that do not mention the queried person, to build a complete system of equations before solving.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Before solving, after parsing the entire problem.
mathgap.example: Ignoring constraints involving unrelated people, leading to an underdetermined system and multiple possible answers.

mathgap.title: Signed More-Than Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: In a clause like 'the number of X has more than Y' that appears within a difference equality, treat it as the signed difference (X - Y), which may be negative; do not assume X > Y.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing statements that equate a 'has more than' expression to another difference.
mathgap.example: Assuming 'the number of Alvena has more than Jo' requires Alvena > Jo and rejecting the equation when Alvena < Jo, instead of writing (Alvena - Jo) = (Yetta - Cassie).

mathgap.title: Factor Increase Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X increases by a/b times' (or 'by N times'), interpret it as a multiplicative scaling: new X = old X * (a/b) (or * N).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering phrases like 'increases by ... times' or 'is increased by ... times'.
mathgap.example: Treating 'Ursula's count increases by 20/19 times' as adding 20/19 to the count or dividing by 20/19, instead of multiplying the original count by 20/19.

mathgap.description: Treating ‘difference between the number of X and Y’ as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model defaults to thinking of 'difference' as a magnitude, ignoring the order of terms.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of the two terms and interpret the phrase as X - Y, preserving sign.

mathgap.description: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model processes transfers after building the system, forgetting that they affect later constraints.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when it appears, before processing subsequent statements that may depend on the updated counts.

mathgap.description: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats direct assignments as immutable, not as current values that can be updated later.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct assignments as setting the current count at that point, which can be altered by later transfers.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting a difference equality as a direct assignment to a single variable, ignoring the second term (including assuming positivity).
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model simplifies (A - B) = (C - D) to A = C - D, dropping B and D, or assumes the left side must be positive.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate the full equality as (A - B) = (C - D), preserving both terms and their signs.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'increases by N times' as addition or division instead of multiplication.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase 'increases by' is often associated with addition, leading the model to add rather than multiply.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Recognize 'increases by ... times' as a multiplicative scaling: multiply the original count by the given factor.
